one_liner: Python code generator for GETT tensor contractions; beats MKL-backed transpose-transpose-GEMM-transpose up to about 2x on bandwidth-bound cases.
what_it_does: TCCG takes a symbolic contraction plus index sizes in a small text file (for example C[a,b,i,j] = A[i,m,a] * B[m,j,b] with a = 24 ...) and emits, compiles and times candidate C++ implementations using three strategies: GETT, TTGT (transpose-transpose-GEMM-transpose on top of BLAS) and LoG (loops over GEMM). It returns the fastest candidate as source code. There is no runtime library API: every new contraction or size means another generate-compile-time cycle, and the output is code you include in your own build.
how_it_is_fast: GETT (GEMM-like Tensor-Tensor multiplication, Springer and Bientinesi, arXiv 1607.00145) applies the BLIS/Goto GEMM blocking directly to tensors: it packs sub-tensors into cache-sized buffers while preserving the stride-one index, then runs an AVX2 or AVX-512 register-blocked macro-kernel, so it never materializes transposed copies the way TTGT does and needs no workspace beyond small tiles. A performance model ranks the blocking and loop-order candidates and the tool then times up to --maxImplementations of them (default 16 for GETT). The gain is largest when the contraction is bandwidth-bound and TTGT's transposes dominate.
when_to_use: Bandwidth-bound contractions of 4- to 6-D tensors with modest index extents (coupled-cluster CCSD, AO2MO style), where TTGT spends much of its time transposing.
Fixed contraction shapes known ahead of time, where offline autotuning per shape and generating code into your build is acceptable.
x86-64 with AVX2 and an Intel compiler plus MKL, the configuration the published results used.
As a reference implementation of GETT packing and macro-kernels to reimplement in your own tensor code.
when_not_to_use: Compute-bound contractions: in the repo's own figures TTGT ties or beats GETT (abcd-aebf-fdec about 67 vs 75 GFLOPS in single precision; TTGT leads on the last four double-precision cases).
Shapes known only at run time, or index sizes where the product of each input's free-index sizes is not a multiple of 24 (the stated GETT limitation).
Anything you need to redistribute: the repository has no license file, so the code is all rights reserved.
Complex numbers or GPUs for GETT: only single and double precision real types (issue #2, 2024, asks for double complex), and CUDA covers only TTGT and LoG.
Modern Python environments: the generator is Python 2 code (print statements, distutils setup.py) last changed in 2017.

integration.dependencies: Python 2.7 for the generator; a BLAS (config.cfg defaults to MKL); the HPTT transposition library; the Makefile's CPU target also links TCL's libtcl.so although the README calls TCL optional; cuBLAS for the CUDA path
integration.min_toolchain: Python 2.7 (tested 2.7.5 and 2.7.9); Intel icpc 15+ recommended or g++ 4.8+ (experimental); generated code built with -std=c++11
integration.platforms: x86-64 AVX2 (AVX-512 experimental); NVIDIA CUDA for TTGT and LoG only (config.cfg sets -arch=sm_30)

gotchas: The performance model hard-codes the authors' Haswell machine in tccg/arch.py (AVX2: 2.5 GHz, 2 FMAs per cycle, 256 KiB L2, 2 x 30 MiB L3, 13 GiB/s axpy bandwidth; AVX-512: 1.3 GHz), so candidate ranking on other CPUs may be off; raise --maxImplementations to time more variants.
Small tiles live on the stack by default; --useDynamicMemory is needed if the stack is too small and the help text warns it may degrade performance.
Tuned solutions are cached in an SQLite database (tccg/tccg.db under TCCG_ROOT) and reused unless --ignoreDatabase is passed.
Thread affinity is left to the user (--affinity sets KMP_AFFINITY or GOMP_CPU_AFFINITY), and the help text warns that a bad choice hurts performance severely.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: TBLIS is the closer sibling and also avoids explicit transposes with a runtime library interface, so prefer it for production; pick TCCG only to study or reproduce GETT, or to autotune a few fixed bandwidth-bound shapes offline. HPTT is the transposition building block that TCCG's TTGT path itself uses, so it complements rather than replaces this.
verified_claims_summary: On one core of an Intel Xeon E5-2680 v3 (Haswell, TurboBoost and SpeedStep off), built with icpc 16.0.1 -O3 -xhost -mkl, the figures (read by eye) show GETT at about 20.5 vs 15 GFLOPS for MKL-backed TTGT on abcde-efbad-cf and about 55.5 vs 25 on abcdef-dfgb-geac in single precision, and TCCG roughly 10x the best of CTF/naive on the most bandwidth-bound cases, with parity or a TTGT lead on compute-bound ones. The TTGT baseline is the authors' own implementation, not a third-party library.
status_note: Abandoned since 2017-08-14 (47 commits, 40 stars, one branch) and unlicensed, so it is reference-only; the same author's TCL library is also unmaintained and points users to NVIDIA cuTENSOR.
